messages:
Maya Chen: Anyone else seeing an unexpected vendor charge for eu-west1 yesterday? Ran a short demo and billing shows ~4 extra H100 hours that I can't map to any pool usage. Tagging @Leo and @vendor-bot

Leo Patel: Which pool/demo id did you use?

Maya Chen: demo burst, pool id `burst-eu-03` — I spun two small jobs, each ~12m. billing shows 4h.

Ashley Gomez: Did you use the dedicated fallback or the hosted tier? Billing can attribute reserved pools differently.

Maya Chen: Hosted demo burst, not Dedicated. I double-checked the run ids: `run-2024-11-07-0932` and `run-2024-11-07-0945`.

Leo Patel: checking fleet logs now. If something fell back to a reserved slot we'd see a start/stop event. give me a minute.

vendor-bot: Invoice 2024-11-08-INV-7789 created for account redwood-demo; 4.00 H100 hours charged; reference: slot-alloc-zz12.

Maya Chen: That invoice id matches what Finance pinged me about. I don't see slot-alloc-zz12 in our recent allocations list.

Ryan Li: Quick check — any chance the test harness used `pin_dedicated: true` in the env? I had a flaky test that accidentally toggled that flag last week.

Maya Chen: Nope, harness config shows `pin_dedicated: false`. pasted snippet below:
```
env: { mode: "burst", pin_dedicated: false, region: "eu-west1" }
```

Leo Patel: I pulled the allocator timeline, looks like at 09:33 we had a transient fallback: `burst-eu-03` failed to provision ephemeral slot -> allocator routed to reserved slot `slot-alloc-zz12` for continuity. The reserved slot auto-attached and held for 3h50m.

Maya Chen: Ah, that explains it. Any reason the allocator couldn't retry other ephemerals first?

Leo Patel: It tries ephemerals, but there was a parallel surge from internal loadtests at that minute. Fallback policy is currently aggressive to avoid request failures.

Ashley Gomez: If that's the case we should either relax fallback or reduce reserved hold window. Happy to file a config PR.

Maya Chen: I can reproduce locally if you want to test changes. Would prefer shorter hold (30m) for burst demos.

oncall-sre: FYI — we saw an allocation spike at 09:33, traced to a nightly job that overlapped with demos. We've paused that job for the next window.

Ryan Li: Proposed short-term fix: change fallback hold to 30m for burst pools and add a quota guard that warns when reserved usage > 1h for demo-tagged runs. I'll draft a PR.

Maya Chen: Sounds good. Can you add an alert to the console too? Low-friction for devs to see when a reserved slot is used.

Leo Patel: Will open PR and include allocator metrics. Assigning to @Ryan for the quota guard.

vendor-bot: Billing note attached to Invoice 2024-11-08-INV-7789: "Auto-attached reserved slot usage; customer-controllable fallback policy can change future behavior."

Maya Chen: OK thanks all. For Finance I can mark this as explainable if we update fallback policy going forward. Leaving this thread for PR follow-ups. :thumbsup:
